headline: UN Creates International Day Against Child Marriage
meta_description: The UN General Assembly unanimously adopted November 27 as an annual International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage.
summary_short: In a unanimous move, the UN General Assembly has established November 27 as an annual International Day dedicated to ending child, early, and forced marriage.
body:
The UN General Assembly has unanimously adopted a resolution designating November 27 as an annual International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The resolution marks a global commitment to addressing a practice that affects millions of young people worldwide.

Around 70 countries co-sponsored the resolution, demonstrating broad international support for action against child marriage. The establishment of a dedicated international day provides a focal point for awareness-raising and advocacy efforts each year, helping to mobilize governments, civil society organizations, and communities around this shared goal.

This unanimous adoption signals that ending child marriage is no longer a fringe concern but a priority recognized across the globe—from wealthy nations to developing countries facing the heaviest burden of the practice.
quick_facts: UN General Assembly voted unanimously on the resolution
November 27 designated as the annual observance date
Addresses child, early, and forced marriage globally
